findings.assertion: On 8 June 1692 a disturbance centered on the Mexico City Plaza Mayor occurred during a shortage of maize; an episode at the municipal alhóndiga triggered the confrontation.
findings.locator: The riot as the expression of an urban government in crisis, Figure 1 and text following it; Gonzalbo abstract

findings.assertion: Accounts disagree in detail about the initial confrontation at the grain exchange: Gonzalbo describes women being struck when protesting the maize shortage; Exbalin describes a pregnant woman collapsing and dying before demonstrators moved toward the town hall.
findings.locator: Exbalin, The riot as the expression of an urban government in crisis, paragraph beginning The trajectory; Gonzalbo abstract

findings.assertion: The June 1692 crowd included Indigenous people as well as mestizos and poorer non-Indigenous residents, so the archival label tumulto de los indios is not an adequate description of all participants.
findings.locator: Exbalin introduction paragraphs on crowd composition; Gonzalbo abstract

findings.assertion: Exbalin reconstructs a route of protest through the Plaza Mayor: the crowd sought the corregidor at the town hall, went toward the archbishop's palace, and approached the viceroy's palace; the route is interpreted as a sequence of attempts to petition authorities.
findings.locator: The riot as the expression of an urban government in crisis, Figure 1 and following three paragraphs

findings.assertion: The 1692 disturbances involved fires and damage at the viceregal palace, city hall and market structures of the Plaza Mayor; the present National Palace should not be represented as an unchanged building from 1692.
findings.locator: Exbalin introduction and section on fires; Gonzalbo abstract

findings.assertion: According to Antonio de Robles as presented by Exbalin, a cathedral-associated religious procession and later preaching in Nahuatl by a cathedral cantor were attempts to pacify participants during the riot.
findings.locator: The weakness of the forces of law and order, two paragraphs beginning It is remarkable and The second initiative; fn 22 cites Robles p. 251

findings.assertion: Exbalin reports that a summary criminal proceeding launched 11 June 1692 resulted within 20 days in 80 defendants tried, with 12 death sentences, 32 forced-labor-and-flogging sentences, and nine flogging-only sentences.
findings.locator: Restoring order, two paragraphs beginning The judicial investigation and The sentences were heavy; fn 32

findings.assertion: Colonial authorities ordered a ban on producing and selling pulque on 19 July 1692, but by 31 July had relaxed the restriction for medicinal white pulque, according to Exbalin's reconstruction.
findings.locator: Restoring order, paragraph beginning We saw that the prohibition of pulque; fns 35–37 AHDF Pulquerías vol. 3719

findings.assertion: In July–August 1692 viceregal measures sought to restrict Indigenous residents' presence and dress in the Spanish city; Exbalin emphasizes that enforcing these boundaries in a mixed urban society was difficult.
findings.locator: Restoring order, paragraphs beginning Among the series of ordinances and The prohibition against wearing; fn 38 AGN Historia vol. 413 fol. 1

findings.assertion: Exbalin describes short-term security measures after the riot, including new cavalry detachments, mixed-race militia companies and patrols; the two cavalry units were dissolved by royal order in 1694.
findings.locator: Restoring order, paragraphs beginning In the afternoon of 9 June and In addition to these two cavalry units; fn 42 AHDF Historia en General vol.1 dossier 1
